actions.justification: Mandatory initial assessment of vital signs to confirm hemodynamic stability and establish baseline for this AF patient with HR 108 and hypertension.
Mandatory per ESC AF guideline — 12-lead ECG must be obtained before any rate control is given. Confirms AF diagnosis and assesses for pre-excitation, ischemia, or other rhythm abnormalities.
Mandatory CHA2DS2-VASc scoring required for anticoagulation risk stratification. Patient has hypertension (1 point minimum), making this critical for determining stroke prevention therapy.
Mandatory lab per current phase. BMP assesses electrolytes, renal function, and other metabolic parameters relevant to AF management and medication safety (e.g., before giving rate control agents).
Mandatory lab per current phase. TSH is essential in new-onset AF to rule out hyperthyroidism as a precipitating cause, per ESC AF guidelines.
Continuous cardiac monitoring is indicated for a patient with AF and HR of 108 to track rate response and detect any hemodynamic deterioration during the assessment phase.

Mandatory per ESC AF guideline: assess anticoagulation need is required during Stable AF - Rate Control phase. CHA2DS2-VASc score has been calculated; now formally assess anticoagulation need to guide therapy.

Rate control is mandatory for stable AF. ECG has already been obtained (obtain_12_lead_ecg completed), so it is safe to give rate control. Beta-blocker is first-line rate control agent per ESC AF guidelines for a patient with hypertension and HR 108.

Patient requests rhythm control strategy; cardiology consultation is appropriate to evaluate suitability for cardioversion or antiarrhythmic therapy after rate control and anticoagulation are addressed.

Guidelines explicitly require ECG before giving rate control (give_rate_control_without_ecg is contraindicated). Although a 12-lead ECG was obtained, ordering a follow-up/confirmatory ECG ensures current rhythm is documented prior to rate control administration, satisfying the mandatory sequence: obtain_12_lead_ecg must precede give_rate_control.

ESC AF guidelines mandate rate control as the initial strategy for stable AF. ECG has been obtained, anticoagulation need has been assessed, and CHA2DS2-VASc has been scored. It is now appropriate to administer rate control therapy. Beta-blocker was already given; this action confirms/completes the rate control order per guideline.

Patient has hypertension (CHA2DS2-VASc ≥1 in male, ≥2 in female) and AF for 3 days. Anticoagulation need has been assessed; initiating anticoagulation is mandated by ESC AF guidelines to reduce thromboembolic risk, especially given symptom duration and planned rhythm control.

Chest X-ray is indicated to evaluate for cardiomegaly, pulmonary congestion, or other structural causes contributing to AF, and to assess baseline cardiopulmonary status before rhythm/rate control strategy.
Echocardiogram is essential in AF workup to evaluate left atrial size, left ventricular function, valvular disease, and to assess suitability for rhythm control strategy as requested by the patient.
Patient requests rhythm control strategy; electrophysiology consultation is appropriate to evaluate candidacy for cardioversion or ablation given ongoing AF for 3 days.
CBC is indicated to assess for anemia, infection, or thrombocytopenia which can affect AF management and anticoagulation safety.
Coagulation studies (PT/INR) are essential to guide anticoagulation therapy and monitor bleeding risk in this AF patient.
Renal function assessment via creatinine is important for dosing of anticoagulants (e.g., NOACs are renally cleared) and rate-control agents in this hypertensive AF patient.
INR monitoring is essential to assess anticoagulation adequacy in AF patient on anticoagulation therapy, guiding ongoing management.
Echocardiogram (transthoracic) helps evaluate for structural heart disease, thrombus, and left ventricular function relevant to rhythm control decisions and cardioversion planning.
NT-proBNP provides assessment of cardiac strain/heart failure status which may influence AF management strategy and anticoagulation decisions.
Order troponin to rule out acute myocardial ischemia as a trigger for new-onset atrial fibrillation, which is clinically indicated even in stable patients with palpitations.

Patient requests rhythm control, has been anticoagulated, and AF duration is known (3 days). Cardioversion is appropriate for rhythm control strategy in stable AF with adequate anticoagulation on board per ESC AF guidelines.
HR remains at 108 bpm despite rate control measures already initiated; adding a calcium channel blocker (e.g., diltiazem) can help achieve better rate control target (<110 bpm) per ESC AF guidelines.
